task.name: Invariant index spike: authoritative project invariants as selective context
task.story_text:
## What

Explore a portable invariant-index mechanism that lets TheForge extract, index, and selectively inject human-governed project invariants from the repository it is operating on.

This is not a TheForge-only doctrine catalog. The mechanism must work for any target project that chooses to mark or configure authoritative invariant sources.

## Why

After the v0.14 knowledge feed-forward loop exists, TheForge will have a way to include relevant prior-run lessons in future context. The next meta-knowledge question is whether stable project invariants can prevent churn: plan regenerations, review cycles, and repeated findings caused by agents missing a rule the project already knows.

Invariants are high-leverage context because they encode "do not break this" constraints compactly. But they are also dangerous if implemented as a second source of truth or selected too narrowly. This spike proves the shape before committing to a broader meta-knowledge substrate.

## Product constraints

- The feature is portable across target projects, not specialized to TheForge's own ADR/convention culture.
- Invariants live in authoritative project-owned docs or configured sources; the extracted index is derived, rebuildable, and disposable.
- The system does not restate invariant prose into a standalone source of truth.
- Scope selection is conservative. If applicability is uncertain, TheForge falls back to broader inclusion rather than guessing small.
- Initial rollout is asymmetric: plan/dev may receive compressed invariant capsules, while review keeps broader context until the approach proves it does not create correlated misses.
- Success is measured by churn reduction, not token reduction. Prompt-size reduction is useful telemetry, not the main value claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- Defines an annotation or source-discovery convention for project invariants that can live inside authoritative docs such as ADRs, `CONVENTIONS.md`, or project-specific policy docs.
- Provides a deterministic extractor that builds a rebuildable invariant index from marked/configured sources.
- The index records invariant identity, source path, source anchor, scope, enforcement level, and applicability metadata without becoming authoritative over the source document.
- Demonstrates selective invariant injection through context assembly for at least one phase, with included/dropped/uncertain decisions visible in the context manifest.
- Demonstrates conservative fallback when scope confidence is low.
- Keeps review broader than plan/dev in the initial proof so a bad scope decision is less likely to affect both producer and reviewer.
- Measures or reports churn-oriented signals for the proof path, such as plan regen, review cycles, or restated findings. Token count may be reported as secondary telemetry.
- Documents the adoption decision: whether to continue, revise, or drop the invariant-index idea after the spike.

## Example

A target project marks an invariant in an ADR:

```md
<!-- forge-invariant id="summaries-advisory" scope="area:audit phase:plan,dev,review" enforcement="review" -->
LLM-generated summaries advise agents; they never drive coordinator control flow.
<!-- /forge-invariant -->
```

The extractor creates a derived index entry pointing back to the ADR. A story touching audit/knowledge code receives that invariant in its plan/dev context capsule. If TheForge cannot determine whether the invariant applies, it includes the broader source instead of silently dropping the rule.

## Non-goals

- No LLM-authored invariant becomes authoritative.
- No standalone `invariants.yaml` that restates project rules as a competing source of truth.
- No speculative knowledge graph or ERD generation.
- No mechanical coordinator decisions based on invariant prose.

## References

- #787
- Depends on #1860.
- #1860
- #1866

- #1847

handoff.summary: Built the invariant-index spike as an opt-in derived metadata layer. A forge-invariant Markdown comment convention marks rules inside the project's own authoritative docs; a deterministic stdlib-light extractor (src/theforge/invariant_index.py) builds .forge/knowledge/invariants/index.yaml holding provenance and applicability metadata only — never the rule prose — rebuilt via forge index --invariants with malformed markers reported as diagnostics rather than exceptions. task/invariant_selector.py decides which invariants reach a phase and how much source comes with them: plan/dev get narrow capsules only when project-declared file globs match a known file list, every low-confidence path widens to the enclosing Markdown section instead of dropping, and review skips the single confident drop so a bad scope tag cannot blind producer and reviewer together. Preflight is refused outright per ADR-0002 clause 5. task/invariant_manifest.py renders included/dropped/uncertain decisions into ContextPack.invariant_context, which the audit writer persists under context_manifests[]. knowledge_invariant_proof.py adds a churn-only proof section (plan regen, review cycles, dev iterations, restated findings) to forge knowledge-report, excluding cost from the claim and defaulting to insufficient_data. docs/plans/1875-invariant-index-spike.md records the convention, the confidence table, the review asymmetry, and a conservative adoption decision.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 of review fixes addressed the single P1: the invariant context manifest recovered an invariant id by splitting the display source string (source.split('#', 1)[1] over '{source_path}#{invariant_id}'). When a project's Markdown path contained a hash, the derived id matched no candidate, so the manifest reported zero invariants included and listed that invariant as dropped under budget_pressure while its text was in the assembled prompt. ContextItem now carries an explicit item_id field (defaulted to None so no existing constructor breaks), set from InvariantCandidate.invariant_id, and a shared _included_ids() helper reads identity off the item instead of re-parsing the label. Swept for the same pattern and found one more instance: prior-run summaries re-derived run ids with source.split(':', 1)[1] over 'knowledge:{run_id}'. Not reachable with today's hex run ids, but the identical fragility, so it now flows through the same helper rather than leaving one occurrence of the pattern behind. InvariantCandidate.source is documented as display-only. Two tests added: an end-to-end regression that indexes an invariant from docs/rules#v2.md and asserts included/dropped are correct, and a unit test pinning the _included_ids contract across both indexed kinds and items that render no indexed entity. Audited every module touched in earlier cycles for identity-by-string-splitting; the only remaining split calls parse the marker's own scope attribute, which is intended.

handoff.summary: Advisory cleanup pass after APPROVE. Fixed the carried P2 in src/theforge/invariant_index.py: body_start_line was open_line + 1, so an opening forge-invariant marker that wraps across lines put its own scope and enforcement attribute lines inside the recorded body span. The rendered capsule trailed those attributes into the prompt, and because the digest was computed over the real offset-based body while the render used the line span, an unchanged source reported source_digest_matches false. The convention's documented example wraps its marker and so do this repo's fixtures, so this was the normal case rather than an edge one. The span now derives from match.end(), and the digest is computed over exactly the line slice consumers re-read, so index and render cannot disagree — that shared-derivation was the real defect, not just the off-by-one. A rule sharing a line with its markers is now a diagnostic ('shares a line with its markers') rather than a guessed span. INVARIANT_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 1 to 2: the field set is unchanged, but a v1 entry's span points into the marker's attributes, so a stale index would render attribute text as the rule; load_invariant_index rejects it and the manifest note prompts a rebuild. Three tests added: multi-line span excludes attribute lines, inline-body diagnostic, and a render-time capsule test asserting exact rule text plus digest freshness. Spike doc records the body-span rule.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The coordinator-decision risk is not fully retired: src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py calls ContextAssembler.assemble() and passes ContextPack.content into build_preflight_prompt(), but Steps 5 and 8 do not explicitly exclude invariant prose from preflight or test that exclusion. Merely limiting the feature to ContextAssembler does not prevent invariant prose from influencing coordinator-driving preflight output.
  Suggestion: Make invariant selection explicitly return disabled/empty context for preflight and add a phase-seam assertion that preflight receives no invariant prose while plan/dev and review retain their intended behavior.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 3 ('adding a new context source can accidentally affect coordinator decisions'). The plan mitigates by confining consumption to ContextAssembler and audit reporting, but no step names preflight explicitly. KnowledgeConfig's own docstring (config/types.py:1250-1254) records that prior-run context is withheld from preflight because preflight output drives coordinator control flow (ADR-0002 clause 5). Step 5 says 'plan/dev' and 'review' but never asserts preflight is excluded, and Step 8's coverage list has no such case.
  Suggestion: In Step 5, gate invariant selection on the same phase allowlist used for PRIOR_RUN_KIND (plan/dev/review only), and add a Step 8 test asserting assemble(phase='preflight') returns an empty invariant_context manifest.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 extends KnowledgeConfig with 'a list of Markdown source globs', but the existing loader at config/load.py:1629-1635 iterates knowledge keys into a dict[str, bool] and raises on any non-bool value. A list-typed field added to the dataclass will be rejected by that loop unless the loop is restructured.
  Suggestion: Parse the glob list on a separate branch (validate list-of-str, reject non-str entries) and keep the bool loop restricted to the boolean gates before constructing KnowledgeConfig.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 and Step 6 add substantial logic to files already near the advisory 600-line module ceiling (CONVENTIONS.md:406): context_assembler.py is 424 lines and knowledge_effectiveness.py is 460.
  Suggestion: Put invariant selection/scope-confidence logic in a sibling module (e.g. src/theforge/task/invariant_selector.py, mirroring prior_run_selector.py) and keep the assembler as the seam only.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 writes to .forge/knowledge/invariants/index.yaml, a new subdirectory under the knowledge storage layout; docs/plans/forge-storage-layout.md is not in any step's file list.
  Suggestion: Add the derived-index path to the storage layout doc in Step 9 so the disposable/rebuildable artifact is recorded alongside summaries and index.yaml.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] ContextPack has many constructors across tests and coordinator stages; adding new fields without safe default values would break backward compatibility. Ensure new fields like invariant_context default to None or an empty dict.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The deterministic extractor must handle malformed invariant comments gracefully without crashing. Ensure the indexer registers diagnostics for skipped or malformed paths rather than throwing unhandled exceptions.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Low-confidence triggers are not explicitly specified. Define concrete fallback criteria (e.g., matching score threshold, missing scope tags, or blank file list) and document them.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
